brief:
Palestinians fleeing their homes after October 7 prioritized irreplaceable personal items over material possessions, according to Al Jazeera English. Displaced residents chose photographs, documents, jewelry, and heirlooms—objects tied to family history and identity rather than monetary value. The selections reflected deep attachments to memory and heritage as people abandoned their lives with minimal warning.

The pattern of what families salvaged offers a window into the human dimensions of displacement across Gaza. People grabbed children's school certificates, wedding rings, and pictures of deceased relatives—tangible links to their pasts. The choices reveal how individuals facing sudden loss navigate impossible decisions about what defines their sense of self and family continuity.
dek: Palestinians displaced by war chose cherished items, revealing poignant stories amid devastation in Gaza.
title: Palestinians carry memories in flight from October 7 war
